method: EAC national public health labs / expert panel (Burundi, Kenya, Rwanda, South Sudan, Tanzania, Uganda)
finding: Progress on sustainable AMR-NAP implementation ranges 7% (Burundi) to 94% (Kenya); WHO AMR-surveillance checklist completion 44-100%; gaps in lab capacity, representativeness, integration and financing
limitations: Qualitative NAP/report synthesis by expert panel; no quantitative outcomes

method: 12 East African studies (2005+, PubMed + AJOL), mostly bloodstream infections
finding: High resistance to first-line drugs 50-100% (ampicillin, cotrimoxazole), emerging ceftriaxone resistance (46-69%) in Gram-negatives, mainly Klebsiella and E. coli; MRSA 2.6-4%
limitations: Small body of heterogeneous studies; not a meta-analysis

method: 469 consecutively enrolled patients, Mnazi Mmoja Hospital, Zanzibar
finding: Pathogenic bacteria in 14% of patients; first report of community-acquired ESBL Enterobacteriaceae bloodstream infections in Zanzibar; 6/7 Salmonella Typhi isolates multidrug resistant
limitations: Single-centre study; small number of ESBL isolates

method: Systematic review 2010-2017, 35 African studies (>60% East Africa)
finding: HCAI driven by Klebsiella, S. aureus, E. coli, Pseudomonas; MRSA 3.9-56.8%; ESBL Gram-negatives 1.9-53%; surveillance sparse
limitations: Heterogeneous primary studies; review not meta-analysis
